prev_agent:
The crashes stem from the preemption hook doing a context switch inside the interrupt frame. When `process_preempt_hook` called `process_yield()` from the timer ISR, we were switching threads while the old thread’s interrupt context was still on the stack—on SMP this corrupts saved contexts (zero RIP, hash mismatches, etc.).

I’ve removed the in-ISR switch. Now `process_preempt_hook` just marks the thread as preempt-pending and returns, so the ISR no longer switches contexts.

Files changed:
- `src/kernel/process.c`: `process_preempt_hook` no longer calls `process_yield`; it simply sets `preempt_pending = true` and exits.

Rebuild succeeded (`make`). With this, SMP should stop corrupting thread contexts. Scheduling will rely on cooperative yields/sleeps; once stable, we can reintroduce safe preemption in a separate ISR-safe path.
